newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia opens door to talks with leftist rebels.
newsitem.headline: Colombia opens door to talks with leftist rebels.

text.p: The government opened the door on Wednesday to direct talks with Colombia's leading leftist guerrilla group to secure the release of at least 60 soldiers held prisoner since last summer.

"The government is going to demonstrate its willingness to reach a bilateral accord over the release (of the soldiers)," said Carlos Vicente de Roux, President Ernesto Samper's special adviser on human rights.
"The government is willing to conciliate," he added.

De Roux, who spoke to reporters after a meeting at the foreign ministry, said the government planned to issue a statement on Thursday in which it would respond formally to a call made earlier this month by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) for direct talks to arrange the handover of the captive soldiers.

The soldiers -- whose number has varied in conflicting accounts by the military and rebels between 64 and 60 -- were taken prisoner on Aug. 31 when FARC commandos overran a remote military base on the banks of the Caqueta River in southwestern Putumayo province. Twenty-seven soliders were killed in the attack, which marked the start of a nationwide rebel offensive and shamed the military high command.

The government ordered the demilitarization of vast tracts of land in the southwest last month as part of a preliminary agreement, brokered by the International Committee of the Red Cross, to win the soldiers' release. But rebel commanders refused to free the captives, citing the army's failure to withdraw from a key area known as Remolinos del Caguan.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, was formed in 1964 as a Marxist-led, pro-Soviet group. Government and military officials say its leaders have long since given up their dreams of a Cuba-style revolution and are dedicated almost exclusively to growing rich through kidnapping, banditry and the protection of rural drug farms and laboratories.
